GPR is capable of estimating the dielectric properties of the lunar regolith, which can then be used to infer its mineralogical and mechanical properties. Traditionally, estimating the electrical permittivity relies on arrival-time inversion, commonly known as hyperbola fitting. This article builds upon hyperbola fitting by suggesting a joint velocity–attenuation inversion. The proposed scheme utilizes not only arrival times but also the wave amplitudes of multiple hyperbolas. In contrast to traditional hyperbola fitting, which is limited to estimating only the permittivity, the proposed scheme extends its capabilities by enabling the estimation of both the permittivity and the electromagnetic losses. This leads to a multitask optimization in which each task is scaled automatically using a homoscedastic loss function. Via this approach, both the electrical permittivity and the attenuation coefficient of the subsurface are simultaneously derived utilizing either a single or multiple hyperbolas.
author: Iraklis Giannakis, Yi Xu, Feng Zhou, Craig Warren, Zhaofa Zeng, Antonios Giannopoulos

title: A Fast Global Contrast Method for Infrared Small–Dim Target Detection
content: The global contrast measure (GCM) has been proven the effective for infrared (IR) small–dim target detection under complex background, especially when the target is not locally salient. However, the reference of current GCM methods is obtained by iterations, which is time-consuming. In this article, a new framework named the fast GCM (FGCM) is proposed, in which the reference is obtained in the frequency domain by multiscale wavelet decomposition and reconstruction without iteration, thus significantly improving the detection speed. Specifically, before FGCM calculation, the idea of a matched filter is adopted on the original image to suppress random noise, and the local max dilation (LMD) operation is applied to the global reference to recover the information of complex background edges (EBs) and corners. Meanwhile, a fan-shaped difference of Gaussians (FDoG) filter is proposed as a weighting function to further suppress clutter. Experimental results on 12 real IR sequences and two public single-frame datasets (SIRST and IRSTD-1k) demonstrate that the proposed method can achieve satisfactory performance in target enhancement and complex background suppression, which in most cases is as good as or only slightly worse than some global methods. Also, compared with existing global contrast methods, its time consumption is much lower, indicating its applicability in certain real-time scenarios. The code of this article is available at: https://github.com/Ice-Cat-Monkey/FGCM.git
author: Jinhui Han, Kai Zhang, Qian Zhao, Lihong Zhang, Minghui Liu, Zeshuo Tian

title: Infrared Small Object Detection Based on Spatial–Frequency Enhancement and Manifold-Constrained Multiresidual Redistribution
content: Infrared small object detection (ISOD) plays an important role in remote sensing and security applications, yet it still faces challenges. Infrared small targets exhibit weak feature responses in the spatial domain, which can be compensated by incorporating frequency-domain information. In addition, the identity mapping in residual connections of existing networks causes the continuous propagation of background features, thereby weakening the representation capability of small targets. To address these issues, we propose a frequency-guided multiresidual manifold redistribution network (FMRNet). Specifically, to tackle the weak response of small targets in the spatial domain, we propose the spatial–frequency modulation (SFM) module. This module uses a lightweight multilayer perceptron (MLP) to adaptively reweight amplitude, highlighting sparse high-frequency target energy, and fuses it with spatial features to improve target separability. To address the excessive propagation of background features in residual connections, we propose the manifold-constrained multiresidual redistribution (MMR) module as the core feature extraction component of FMRNet. This module constructs multilevel, multiscale feature streams through multiple bottleneck blocks and maps residual connection space onto the manifold of doubly stochastic matrices to dynamically redistribute multiresidual streams, thereby effectively suppressing the propagation of redundant background features. To address information loss caused by downsampling, we propose the high-fidelity parallel downsampling (HPD) module. This module enhances semantic and spatial features via convolutional and pooling branches, with concatenated outputs expanding channels and retaining more target information. Experimental results show that our method outperforms state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods on public datasets.
author: Bin Xiao, Yue Hu

title: FBAP-Net: A Frequency-Band-Aware Amplitude–Phase Network for Precipitation Nowcasting
content: The coupling between structural motion and intensity evolution remains a major challenge in radar echo nowcasting, often causing boundary blurring, structural drift, and attenuation of high-reflectivity echo cores. Although amplitude–phase disentanglement provides a promising frequency-domain perspective, existing methods usually model the phase spectrum in a coarse-grained manner and overlook the heterogeneous structural characteristics across different frequency regions. To address this issue, this article proposes a frequency-band-aware amplitude–phase forecasting framework for radar echo nowcasting. Specifically, FB-Hybrid PhaseNet partitions the phase spectrum into low-, mid-, and high-frequency bands and captures multiscale structural dynamics through hybrid attention and hierarchical gated fusion. The spatiotemporal amplitude network (ST-AmpliNet) provides intensity-aware compensation by modeling temporal intensity trends and multiscale spatial variations. The amplitude–phase mixer further coordinates the amplitude-driven and phase-driven predictions through low-frequency amplitude–phase recombination and spatial-domain refinement. Experiments on CIKM 2017 and Shanghai 2020 demonstrate that the proposed method maintains competitive performance at general precipitation thresholds and shows clear advantages over the compared baselines on several high-reflectivity metrics. The results indicate that frequency-band-aware phase modeling and amplitude–phase coordination effectively improve the detection and preservation of high-reflectivity echo regions, making the proposed framework effective for moderate-to-heavy precipitation nowcasting.
author: Yu Xue, Xinyu Zhang, Mohamed Wahib, Peng Chen

title: Small-Sample Space Target Recognition Based on Polarimetric Scattering Mechanisms and Geometric Features
content: Space target recognition (STR) plays a crucial role in ensuring space security. However, existing methods exhibit insufficient exploitation of polarimetric information, limited robustness to angular variations, and heavy reliance on large-scale labeled data. To address these issues, inspired by the attributed scattering center (ASC), we propose a method that jointly exploits the physical scattering properties and geometric features for target recognition under limited training samples. To characterize scattering behavior, both the scattering mechanism and the diversity of polarimetric descriptions are important; therefore, polarimetric features are explored from two aspects. First, we design a collaborative attention mechanism that dynamically integrates polarimetric signatures with dominant scattering mechanisms to enhance the representation of discriminative scattering centers. Second, to alleviate cross-angle sensitivity, a subspace polarimetric descriptor is introduced to characterize the coherence statistics under different polarization states. Finally, the geometric contour features extracted by a shallow convolutional neural network (CNN) from binarized images are used to provide complementary structural priors for the physical scattering features. Experiments on the polarimetric space target dataset demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior performance by effectively integrating scattering features and geometric priors within a lightweight architecture. Compared with existing methods, the proposed method achieves improvements of 10.91% and 16.3% in the 1-shot setting for the same-angle and cross-angle evaluations, respectively, and 1.24% and 3.87% in the 3-shot setting.
author: Wenhao Xiao, Junjun Yin, Jian Yang

title: Information Bottleneck-Guided Enhancement of Decomposition-Derived Scattering Features for PolSAR Image Classification
content: Model-based polarimetric target decomposition derives physically interpretable scattering features from predefined scattering models and has been widely used for polarimetric synthetic aperture radar (PolSAR) image classification. However, the idealized assumptions of these models may be inconsistent with real PolSAR targets, especially when man-made structures are not aligned with the radar line of sight. This mismatch can lead to scattering ambiguity in decomposition-derived features, weakening feature discriminability and physical interpretability, and thereby restricting data-driven PolSAR classification. To address this issue, an information bottleneck-guided plug-and-play framework is proposed to enhance decomposition-derived scattering features. The framework couples semantic discrimination with physics-guided scattering constraints, thereby connecting deep discriminative feature learning with physically interpretable modeling without introducing additional scattering models. Experiments on multiple airborne and spaceborne PolSAR datasets demonstrate clearer class separation, more physically consistent scattering behavior, and improved classification performance.
author: Zhaoquan Wang, Di Zhuang, Lamei Zhang, Bin Zou, Wataru Takeuchi

title: SMESP-DiffDet: Small-Object MoE Enhanced Spatial Prior-Guided DiffDet for Visible-Infrared Object Detection
content: Small-object detection remains highly challenging due to their small size, weak texture, and severe environmental interference, even when both visible and infrared modalities are used, especially in remote sensing images. To address this issue, this article proposes small-object MoE-enhanced spatial prior-guided DiffDet (SMESP-DiffDet) for visible–infrared object detection, which incorporates two key components: the small-object MoE enhancement (SME) module and the spatial prior-guided box renewal strategy (SP-BRS). Specifically, unlike existing mixture-of-expert (MoE) models that rely on implicit experts, the SME module introduces dedicated experts for small-object detection to enhance localization and classification accuracy by capturing more discriminative feature representations of small objects. This process is further guided by a small-object constraint loss. Based on this, instead of supplementing random proposal boxes during diffusion decoding, the proposed SP-BRS leverages the small-object spatial priors learned in SME to guide the candidate box renewal process, providing potential small-object regions for decoding and thus improving detection accuracy and efficiency. Extensive experiments on three representative public datasets demonstrate that SMESP-DiffDet significantly improves visible–infrared small-object detection performance, achieving up to approximately 2.5% improvement in mAP50 compared with state-of-the-art methods.
author: Zian Wang, Puhong Duan, Jin Yuan, Xudong Kang, Zhiyong Li

title: Cross-Domain Hyperspectral Target Detection Based on Physical Constraints and Spectral Generation
content: To address the problems of significant spectral scale differences between multispectral images (MSIs) and hyperspectral images (HSIs), strong spectral variability of targets, and insufficient collaborative utilization of spatial–spectral features in cross-domain hyperspectral target detection (HTD), this article proposes a physically constrained spectral generation (SG) and dual-stream spatial–spectral fusion network for HTD (PSG-HTD). PSG-HTD comprises three parts. First, a cross-domain spectral self-attention (CSSA) mechanism is introduced to model long-range cross-band dependencies between MSIs and HSIs. Second, PSG-HTD incorporates a standard spectral library as a physical prior to improve the semantic rationality and physical credibility of generated spectra. Third, an adaptive dual-stream spatial–spectral extraction (ADSSE) module jointly exploits spectral discriminative and spatial structural features for cross-domain HTD. Experimental results demonstrate strong performance in both SG and cross-domain HTD tasks: 1) for SG, PSG-HTD reduces the root-mean-square error (RMSE) by up to 71.0% and improves the peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) by about 37.4% over comparison methods, indicating that embedding physical constraints effectively alleviates the spectral distortion problem and ensures physical credibility and 2) for cross-domain HTD, it achieves the highest mAP@0.5 of 0.917 and 0.714 on RarePlanes and RSOD-VHR10, respectively, indicating that high-fidelity SG provides robust, domain-invariant features that significantly enhance downstream cross-domain target identification capability. This study provides a new idea for SG and cross-domain HTD, and has important application potential in the fields of fine recognition and accurate classification of remote sensing targets.
author: Zijin Li, Boya Zhao, Yuanfeng Wu, Bing Zhang

title: HCD2: A Generative Dense Classification Framework for Hyperspectral Imagery With Conditional Diffusion
content: Hyperspectral image (HSI) classification aims to recover accurate land-cover semantic distributions from high-dimensional spectral–spatial observations remaining a critical pillar in intelligent Earth observation. Existing models, such as the convolutional neural networks (CNNs), the Transformers, and the Mamba are predominantly based on discriminative learning paradigms, which often struggle to effectively model the underlying spectral–spatial distributions of ground objects under complex noise, spectral mixing, and intraclass spectral variability. To address the limitations, a hyperspectral conditional diffusion for dense (HCD2) classification framework is proposed in this article, which reformulates HSI classification as a conditional label-map denoising process guided by hyperspectral features, enabling generative dense semantic inference. Specifically, in the encoding stage, an adaptive spectral decoupling (ASD) module is designed to enhance class-discriminative spectral representations. Furthermore, a spatial–spectral joint topological encoder (SSJTE) is constructed to jointly model long-range spatial dependencies and spectral topological structures, thereby learning robust spectral–spatial representations. In the decoding stage, a conditional diffusion category decoder (CDCD) is proposed to achieve semantic category restoration and progressive refinement through conditional diffusion and iterative denoising. Experiments on several public datasets demonstrate that the proposed HCD2 consistently outperforms existing discriminative and generative methods, while exhibiting robustness in complex scenarios.
author: Hongqiao Wang, Haiyan Sun, Xuanchen Yan, Yanping Cai, Zhaoxiang Zhang

title: Learning to Expand and Align: A Fourier-Based Vision–Language Framework for Incremental Hyperspectral Image Classification
content: With the rapid increase in satellite data acquisition, efficient adaptation to newly acquired hyperspectral scenes has become increasingly important. In this context, incremental learning provides a practical solution by enabling models to continuously learn new knowledge without retaining all historical data or performing full retraining. However, substantial distribution shifts across sensors, acquisition conditions, and imaging environments significantly limit the ability of existing methods to adapt from a labeled base scene to a newly acquired scene under few-shot supervision. Moreover, the cosine similarity-based prediction has difficulty capturing higher order statistical information and complex data relationships, which are important for improving classification performance. To address these challenges, we propose a Fourier-based vision–language framework for incremental hyperspectral image classification (HSIC), learning to expand and align (LEAF). In the base session, a Fourier-based domain expansion (FDE) strategy generates expanded domains to facilitate domain-invariant feature learning. To further enhance representation capability, a multilevel vision–language alignment module aligns visual and textual embeddings at both instance and class levels. During the inference stage, a covariance-enhanced prediction (CEP) strategy incorporates second-order statistical information to improve prediction robustness and reliability. Extensive experiments on three benchmark hyperspectral datasets demonstrate that the LEAF consistently achieves superior overall performance over state-of-the-art methods in incremental HSI classification (HSIC) tasks. The code will be available at https://github.com/ZhangYun123zy/TGRS_2026_LEAF
author: Yun Zhang, Bobo Xi, Jiaojiao Li, Hongsheng Zhang, Yunsong Li, Wei Xiang

title: Adaptive Boundary Consistency Learning for Open-Set Semi-Supervised Hyperspectral Image Classification
content: Most existing semi-supervised hyperspectral classification methods are built upon the closed-set assumption, which assumes that unlabeled samples originate exclusively from the known class space. However, this assumption is frequently invalid in real-world remote sensing scenarios. In addition, hyperspectral images (HSIs) exhibit complex spectral–spatial characteristics, facing challenges such as complex spatial boundaries, significant interclass spectral similarity, and intraclass variability. To address these issues, this article proposes an adaptive boundary consistency learning (ABCL) model for open-set semi-supervised HSI classification, which achieves low-cost and high-accuracy perception while also considering known-class classification and unknown-class rejection. First, to enhance the model’s ability to represent complex land-cover boundaries and spatial structural differences, an anisotropic position transformer (APT) is designed to introduce direction-sensitive spatial priors by decoupling horizontal and vertical positional biases. Second, to address interference from unknown classes in a large number of unlabeled samples, an adaptive entropy mask (AEM) is proposed to guide consistency learning, thereby improving the discriminability of the model’s features. Finally, to further optimize the feature space structure, a category recognition module (CRM) is introduced. By enhancing intraclass compactness and interclass separability, it provides a more stable representation basis for open-set discrimination. Experimental results on three public hyperspectral datasets, Indian Pines (IP), Salinas (SA), and LN02, demonstrate that with only ten labeled samples per known class, the overall accuracy (OA) of the proposed method reaches 79.56%, 88.20%, and 96.15%, respectively. Furthermore, the model exhibits stable advantages in metrics such as unknown, average accuracy (AA), and Kappa coefficient, outperforming various representative state-of-the-art methods. This study provides a low-cost, high-precision technical foundation with strong adaptability to unknown classes for target perception in HSIs.
author: Huaping Zhou, Shuai Xu, Man Chen, Kelei Sun, Yongjie Huang, Xiangyu Yang, Ling Jiang, Hanwen Liu

title: Coupled Registration and Change Detection for Remote Sensing Images: A Joint Optimization Framework
content: This article addresses a fundamental limitation in remote sensing image analysis: the error propagation caused by treating registration and change detection as independent sequential tasks. We propose a novel end-to-end joint learning framework that establishes bidirectional coupling between these two tasks, enabling mutual enhancement through shared optimization. The key insight is that registration quality directly impacts detection accuracy, while change detection feedback can guide more semantically meaningful alignment. To realize this joint optimization, we design a unified architecture where a contrastive learning-based module projects multitemporal images into a modality-invariant feature space, a graph-based regression module exploits spatial relationship priors for robust displacement prediction, and a generative adversarial detection module with global attention captures long-range semantic dependencies. Crucially, these components are connected through a multitask loss function that simultaneously optimizes structural consistency for registration and discriminative feature learning for detection, breaking the traditional pipeline’s error accumulation. Experiments on four benchmark datasets demonstrate that this joint optimization paradigm significantly outperforms both traditional sequential approaches and state-of-the-art individual methods, achieving  $F1$ -scores of 93.10%, 90.60%, 95.46%, and 89.65% on WHU-CD, CDD, LEVIR-CD+, and Greenhouse Change Detection dataset (GHCD), respectively, validating that synergistic learning between registration and detection yields superior performance for handling geometric distortions and multitemporal heterogeneity.
author: Jiaxin Lu, Liangzhi Li, Tingyu Zhang, Gaoxiang Zhou, Kyle Gao, Zongfan Bai, Zongyi Liu

title: UniCIC: A Unified Collaborative Inference Framework for Remote Sensing Change Detection and Captioning
content: Multilevel change interpretation (MCI) aims to jointly model change detection (CD) and change captioning (CC) within a unified framework, integrating pixel-level localization and semantic-level description to achieve multigranularity change understanding. However, existing MCI methods suffer from two critical drawbacks: 1) they lack a mechanism to separately capture fine-grained spatial cues for CD and object-level semantic cues for CC during feature encoding and 2) they lack effective cross-task interaction mechanisms, which severely restricts the collaborative performance gain. To address these issues, we propose unified collaborative inference framework (UniCIC) that constructs heterogeneous change representations from bitemporal images for different tasks and enables cross-task collaborative inference. Specifically, we propose an SAM-prior-guided task-oriented perception encoding (SP-TOPE) module, which employs an SAM-based region-level perception frame to capture the object-level semantics required for CC and introduces a randomly initialized perception frame to aggregate the fine-grained spatial change cues required for CD, leveraging the cross-frame modeling capability of a video encoder to generate task-oriented change representations. Furthermore, we design a spatial–semantic mutual guidance ( $\text {S}^{2}\text {MG}$ ) mechanism, which establishes a sequential cross-task interaction pathway by first using a coarse change mask to provide spatial priors for caption generation and then feeding semantic entities extracted from the generated description back into the detection branch to refine the final change mask, thereby improving the consistency between change localization and semantic description. Comprehensive evaluations on the LEVIR-MCI dataset show that the proposed method achieves competitive results in both CD and CC metrics. The code is avaliable at https://github.com/Jiahuiqu/UniCIC.
author: Xintong Cao, Wenqian Dong, Jiahui Qu, Yunsong Li, Qian Du

title: TATF: Toward Diverse and Thermal-Aware Aerial Visible-to-Infrared Image Translation Framework
content: Existing visible-to-infrared image translation methods primarily focus on style transfer and domain mapping. Although some approaches improve generation diversity, they often neglect the physical properties of infrared imagery, particularly the consistency of thermal radiation distributions, and fail to preserve coherent thermal structures. Consequently, the generated images may deviate from realistic thermal structures. To address these issues, we propose a thermal-aware translation framework (TATF) that explicitly incorporates thermal structural constraints into the generation process to enhance physical consistency and structural stability. Specifically, we first introduce a thermal estimation network (TEN) to estimate the relative thermal distribution, which provides auxiliary guidance and enables pixel-level brightness modulation. A thermal structural consistency (TSC) loss is further designed to preserve intrinsic thermal relationships during cross-modal translation. In addition, we propose a wavelet-based patch discriminator (WBPD) that performs fine-grained discrimination across multiple wavelet subbands, enforcing structural consistency in different frequency domains. Finally, a diversity-guided loss (DGL) is incorporated to enable controllable and diverse generation at inference time while maintaining physically reasonable thermal distributions. Extensive experiments on three aerial datasets demonstrate that the proposed method significantly improves both realism and generation diversity, outperforming existing state-of-the-art methods.
author: Zhe Guo, Lan Wei, Rui Luo, Jiayi Liu, Shaohui Mei

title: GeoMEx-VLM: A Geo-Memory Guided Sparse Expert Vision–Language Model for Multigranularity Asset Grounding in Remote Sensing
content: Remote sensing (RS) vision–language models (VLMs) have advanced instruction-following interpretation for captioning, VQA, dialog, and grounding. However, fine-grained remote sensing interpretation remains challenging because objects are often small, densely distributed, rotated, occluded, or visually similar to surrounding infrastructure. Existing RS-VLMs mainly rely on dense shared reasoning, coarse spatial outputs, or limited box-level grounding, restricting their ability to jointly support scene understanding, counting, axis-aligned bounding box (AAB) grounding, rotation-aware bounding box (RAB) localization, and mask prediction. To address these limitations, we propose a geo-memory-guided sparse expert VLM (GeoMEx-VLM) for multigranularity RS interpretation and strategic asset grounding. GeoMEx-VLM introduces a class-scale geo-memory (CSGM) module to retrieve class- and scale-aware geospatial priors and inject them into visual token modeling and sparse expert routing. A geo-memory-guided router assigns tokens to experts using token features, task embeddings, and retrieved geo-context, enabling class-aware and task-adaptive reasoning. Unified spatial tokenization further represents AABs, RABs, and compressed masks as language-compatible outputs within a single autoregressive decoder. Experiments demonstrate high performance on multigranularity RS interpretation, achieving 82.36 Pr@0.5 on DIOR-RSVG language-conditioned horizontal grounding and 75.42 mIoU on referring segmentation, with strong performance on rotation-aware localization, visual question answering, and strategic asset counting. These results validate the effectiveness of geo-memory-guided sparse reasoning and unified spatial tokenization for precise strategic asset understanding. The code is available at https://github.com/umeraza/remote_sensing
author: Hessa Alfraihi, Umar Raza Mukhtar, Hamza Mukhtar

title: GME: A Multigranularity Attention and Mamba-Driven Approach for Underwater Image Enhancement
content: In complex underwater environments, the selective absorption of light by the water medium severely impairs scene context and color fidelity, leading to distorted information and imbalanced colors in the acquired underwater images. Such degradations pose substantial challenges to underwater image enhancement (UIE). In this article, we propose a multiscale U-shaped network termed GME to achieve more effective UIE. Specifically, GME includes three essential components: 1) an enhancement layer (EL) with a group-mix attention (GMA) module that characterizes short-range local textures and medium-range regional context through grouped feature partitioning and mixed multigranularity matching to capture local and regional dependencies at multiple granularities for fine-detail recovery; 2) an enhancement block (EB) consists of a visual state-space (VSS) module and a squeeze-and-excitation (SE) unit which constructs input-aware state transitions to encode global contextual information and learns channel attention weights to reweight the feature channels, thus modeling the long-range spatial interactions and recalibrating the channel responses effectively; and 3) an adaptive enhancement module (AEM) that learns region-aware modulation coefficients to differentiate flat areas, edges, or complex regions modulates the residual enhancement strength adaptively to suppress over-enhancement artifacts in the challenging regions. Extensive experiments on multiple underwater image benchmarks show that GME achieves superior quantitative performance over state-of-the-art UIE methods and delivers visually more natural contrast and color appearance. The source code is available at https://github.com/OUC-AI/GME
author: Jingchao Cao, Hongqing Liu, Yutao Liu, Junyu Dong, Ke Gu, Guangtao Zhai, Sam Kwong

title: Instance-Aware Visible-to-Infrared Image Translation via Spatially Gated Hierarchical Semantic Embeddings
content: Visible-to-infrared (VIS-to-IR) image translation, which synthesizes IR images from VIS counterparts, offers an efficient and scalable solution for thermal IR remote sensing imaging. Currently, mainstream approaches predominantly rely on global domain translation without awareness of individual ground objects. However, such a holistic mapping strategy often leads to physical contradictions in thermal radiation mechanisms and severe radiometric inconsistencies across different object instances in complex remote sensing scenes. To address this issue, an instance-aware VIS-to-IR image translation framework (INVIT) is proposed, which fundamentally breaks the bottleneck inherent in holistic mapping by incorporating fine-grained semantic priors into the generation process. Our key insight is to leverage the Segment Anything Model 2 (SAM2) to extract hierarchical, instance-level semantic embeddings, which are then deeply fused into a multiscale generator. Crucially, we introduce a spatially gated fusion module (SGFM) that adaptively learns spatial weight maps to dynamically regulate the integration of semantic and visual features, ensuring the generation of accurate thermal characteristics for foreground instances while preserving the integrity of background structures. Extensive experiments on standard benchmarks demonstrate that our method outperforms a series of state-of-the-art (SOTA) approaches, validating its superiority in both image-level quantitative metrics and downstream task-level performance.
author: Zonghao Han, Fangqi Shi, Zixiang Ye, Zhengtao Chen, Xiaoning Chen, Shaohui Mei

title: Large Vision Model-Guided Masked Low-Rank Approximation for Ground-Roll Attenuation
content: Ground roll is a common type of coherent noise in seismic records, and its attenuation remains challenging due to its substantial overlap with useful reflections in localized regions. Previous attenuation methods can be broadly classified into global and local categories according to whether ground-roll-contaminated regions are explicitly identified. Global methods, however, typically impose uniform attenuation on both contaminated and uncontaminated regions, which may result in signal leakage or distortion of reflections. By contrast, local methods restrict attenuation to contaminated regions and are therefore less prone to unnecessary modification of clean areas. However, their performance is often limited by manually designed or simplistic model-based mask estimation strategies. To address these limitations, we propose a large vision model-guided masked low-rank approximation (LVM-LRA) framework for ground-roll attenuation. Within this framework, a promptable LVM is first employed to identify ground-roll-dominant regions in seismic records through multimodal prompting and to generate accurate, fine-grained masks. The estimated masks are then incorporated into an LRA model for ground-roll attenuation. A global low-rank constraint is imposed on the reflection component to preserve event continuity, whereas a mask-guided local low-rank constraint is imposed on the ground-roll component so that its separation is confined to the masked regions. An iterative optimization algorithm based on the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) is further developed to solve the resulting model efficiently. Experiments on synthetic and field datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves more effective ground-roll attenuation and better suppresses signal leakage than the baseline methods.
author: Jiacheng Liao, Feng Qian, Yongjian Guo, Ziyin Fan

title: Improving Near-Borehole Reflection Imaging and Slowness Estimation Using 3-D Wavefield Decomposition of Acoustic Logging Data
content: Acoustic logging data are typically dominated by strong direct waves propagating along the borehole, which obscure the weak yet valuable reflected signals needed for near-borehole imaging. Moreover, accurate slowness picking for direct waves can be challenging because of interference from reflected and transmitted waves. Robust decomposition of different wave components is therefore a prerequisite for improving both reflection imaging and velocity analysis. We propose a novel wave decomposition method based on a 3-D sparse Radon transform combined with semblance analysis and a Hilbert autocorrelator. The method separates overlapping wave modes in acoustic logging data by exploiting their distinct slowness and directional characteristics in both common-shot and common-offset gathers. The workflow first maps the data into a high-dimensional sparse domain, where different wave modes become more separable. It then uses semblance analysis to estimate the slowness of dominant linear events in the common-shot domain, followed by dip estimation of direct waves in the common-offset domain using a Hilbert autocorrelator method. These orientation attributes guide a 3-D mask function for selectively isolating direct and reflected waves, including upgoing and downgoing reflections. Each component is then reconstructed in the time–space domain through an inverse Radon transform. Applications to field monopole and dipole datasets demonstrate that the method significantly improves signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), preserves coherent energy, and enables high-fidelity separation of physically meaningful wave modes. In monopole data, P waves, S/pseudo-Rayleigh waves, Stoneley waves, and reflected waves are isolated; in dipole data, flexural and reflected waves are clearly separated. The extracted reflections improve near-borehole imaging, and using only direct waves for slowness estimation greatly improves semblance continuity and focus.
author: Lu Liu, Thierry Tonellot, Hussain Salim, Abdulmohsen Alali

title: Diff-SpaFormer: Efficient Seismic Data Interpolation via Diffusion-Enhanced Sparse Attention Transformer
content: Seismic data interpolation is a critical preprocessing step for improving seismic imaging quality and remains a focus of academic innovation. To address the computational inefficiencies caused by extensive iterative resampling in current plug-and-play diffusion interpolation methods, we propose the diffusion-enhanced sparse attention transformer (Diff-SpaFormer), a novel deep learning framework. Our model integrates transformer architectures and diffusion models via a seismic prior extraction network (SPEN), which serves as a bridge module. Full-layer sparse multihead attention and feed-forward propagation capture global information distributions, while the diffusion model provides robust prior guidance. To mitigate the computational burden of high-dimensional representations, self-attention is computed along the channel rather than the spatial dimension. We show that using negative squared Euclidean distance to compute sparse affinity matrices better suits seismic data modeling, enabling broader contribution from amplitude feature nodes. An adaptive rectified linear unit (ReLU) function further discards low or irrelevant self-attention values. We conduct training within a single-stage optimization framework, requiring only a few reverse diffusion sampling steps during inference. Extensive experiments demonstrate improved interpolation fidelity and computational efficiency for both random and continuous missing data, offering a new paradigm for high-efficiency seismic data reconstruction under complex geological conditions. Furthermore, experiments on field data under local strong noise, low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), and severe interference conditions further validate the robustness and generalization capability.
author: Xiaoli Wei, Chunxia Zhang, Baisong Jiang, Anxiang Di, Deng Xiong, Changpeng Wang, Jiangshe Zhang, Mingming Gong

title: Full-Waveform Inversion Using Progressive Geological Guidance and Learned Waveform Matching
content: The full-waveform inversion (FWI) is highly sensitive to cycle skipping, local minima, and nonuniqueness, particularly when the starting model is smooth and seismic observations provide limited constraints on the subsurface velocity. As a result, waveform matching alone may lead to models that are kinematically acceptable but geologically unreliable. In this study, we propose progressive geology-guided neural (PGGNeural) FWI framework that combines a Siamese representation-based data misfit with sparse well calibration and dip-guided structural regularization. The learned misfit compares observed and simulated shot gathers in a feature space, while the well and dip constraints provide local velocity control and structural guidance during model updating. The proposed framework progressively updates the structural dip guidance as the velocity model evolves, with a weaker dip contribution in the first step and stronger guidance in subsequent steps to stabilize the inversion. Experiments on the British Petroleum (BP) salt and Marmousi models show that PGGNeural produces more accurate and geologically coherent velocity models than benchmarks, with reduced coherent data residuals and improved reverse time migration (RTM) imaging responses. The analyses of progressive updating and well control settings further illustrate how geological guidance improves the stability of the inversion pathway and the recovery of complex salt and layered structures. The proposed framework provides a practical way to improve the convergence behavior and geological reliability of neural FWI by combining learned waveform matching with progressive geological constraints.
author: Liuqing Yang, Min Bai, Dong Zhang, Zixiang Zhou, Xufa Zheng, Hang Xu, Yatong Zhou

title: Systematic Validation of GNSS-R Wind Retrievals From the 22-Satellite Tianmu-1 Constellation Over Chinese Coastal Waters: Multi-GNSS, Intersatellite, and Rainfall Impacts
content: The Tianmu-1 constellation, China's first commercial LEO meteorological satellite system based on GNSS-R, retrieves high spatiotemporal sea surface wind speed by integrating four GNSS signals (GPS, BDS, GAL, GLO). However, systematic validation of its wind products over China's complex coastal waters remains lacking. This study conducts a comprehensive validation using 54,990 collocated matchups between Tianmu-1 retrievals and 31 in-situ buoys, supplemented by 6,341 tropical cyclone matchups with AMSR2 wind and rain data. Key results: (1) The product shows robust performance (bias = 0.34 m/s, RMSE = 1.91 m/s, \(R\) = 0.85). GPS attains the highest accuracy (RMSE = 1.82 m/s), while BDS yields the largest dataset (n = 20,465). SNR bin-wise and incidence-anglecontrolled comparisons reveal that GLO’s larger deviations arise from its FDMA signal scheme and nonlinear GMF mismatch rather than signal strength or geometry. (2) Intersatellite heterogeneity is pronounced: the only linear-polarization satellite (TM11) achieves comparable accuracy (RMSE = 1.69 m/s) to the 21-satellite LHCP group (RMSE = 1.89 m/s). Regional variability is significant (best in Yellow/Bohai Seas, RMSE \(\approx\) 1.63 m/s; worst in South China Sea, RMSE = 2.13 m/s, \(R\) = 0.79). (3) Wind speed-dependent errors exist (overestimation below 2 m/s, underestimation above 14 m/s). (4) Under tropical cyclones, GPS/GAL remain stable (RMSE = 3.45/3.85 m/s), while RMSE rises from 2.25 to 5.17 m/s with increasing rainfall; bootstrap resampling confirms this degradation is physically driven rather than a statistical artifact. This study provides critical insights for GNSS-R algorithm optimization and operational applications over China’s coastal waters.
author: Xiaohui Li, Feixiong Huang, Xinhai Han, Jingsong Yang, Jiuke Wang, He Wang, Guoqi Han, Weiqiang Li

title: Scale-Aware Multiwell Clustering of Multivariate Logging Data for Lithology Identification
content: Multivariate well-log data are important in situ geophysical sensing records for characterizing subsurface formations and supporting lithology identification. However, geological layers often exhibit significant variations in thickness and lithology, including thin interbeds and thick continuous formations, making unsupervised lithology recognition challenging. To address the limitations of conventional clustering methods in simultaneously characterizing interlog conditional dependencies and vertical continuity, this study proposes a scale-aware multiwell Toeplitz inverse covariance-based clustering method (SAM-TICC) for unsupervised lithology identification from multivariate well-log data. The proposed method first extends the standard TICC to a multiwell setting, enabling the joint learning of lithological structural patterns shared across different wells. Continuous wavelet transform is then used to extract local multiscale responses from well-log curves, which are further mapped to a depth-adaptive smoothing parameter to regulate the transition cost between adjacent depth windows. When logging responses are smooth, the model imposes a stronger vertical continuity constraint; when local high-frequency energy is enhanced, the model allows more flexible cluster-label transitions, improving the identification of thin interbeds and lithological boundaries. Experiments on synthetic and field well-log datasets show that the proposed method improves the identification of both thin and thick layers while preserving layer continuity, outperforming baseline clustering approaches. The clustering results are also interpretable, providing insights into lithology distribution and supporting data-driven subsurface characterization.
author: Zijian Wang, Yanfei Wang

title: Waveform Analysis of Super-Resolved WISDOM/ExoMars GPR Data Acquired in Svalbard, a Terrestrial Analogue of Mars
content: The analysis of the waveform of reflection in ground penetrating radar (GPR) data is widely used to determine the nature of interfaces in the subsurface. It is of the utmost importance that the water ice subsurface deposits observation on Mars (WISDOM) GPR onboard Rosalind Franklin rover be able to determine the nature of the interfaces, which can provide information on the density, porosity, and, therefore, the composition of the subsurface layers, and avoid hazards that may damage the drill onboard the ExoMars rover. This article presents validations using numerical simulation and measures in a controlled environment of qualitative and quantitative analysis of the received radar waveforms after application of a super-resolution technique for WISDOM [the bandwidth extrapolation (BWE) technique] to improve identification of the nature of interfaces in the subsurface. The qualitative analysis consists in visual comparison of the reflection waveforms to a reference reflection waveform, allowing a quick but human biased review of different reflections in radargrams. The quantitative analysis is the automatic measurement of the phase value of received radar waveforms to classify it into four meaningful phase values corresponding to four different types of interface: high permittivity material overlying a low permittivity material and vice versa, and thin layer of higher or lower permittivity than the embedding material. The thin bed that can be characterized by WISDOM is 1–4 cm thick in standard data and 0.5–2 cm thick in BWE data. The BWE greatly improves qualitative and quantitative analysis by making the waveform of reflections easier to identify, along with an increased contrast and improved range resolution in radargrams. The quantitative analysis of BWE data is highly effective and reliable on realistic Lunar or Martian rough surface and buried interface, and not strongly affected by volume scattering under heterogeneous conditions. In high loss dispersive media (highest estimated loss for Martian analogue materials), the range of application of the method can be restricted to the first meter in the subsurface. In the case of moderate or low loss (representative of Lunar regolith or Martian analogue materials), this range extend beyond the 2 m deep drilling capacity of the ExoMars rover. The method is also tested on data acquired during a field test campaign in Svalbard (Arctic Norway), and provide useful interpretations of radar reflections on an ice cave and on an icing in a frozen riverbed.
author: Emile Brighi, Valérie Ciarletti, Alice Le Gall, Nicolas Oudart, Wolf-Stefan Benedix, Esther Mas I sanz, Aleksey Shestov, Dirk Plettemeier, Yann Hervé

title: AI-Based Reconstruction of Eddy-Resolved Subsurface Currents in the Indo-Pacific Convergence Zone
content: Nonequilibrium processes are prevalent in the ocean and play a dominant role in governing energy exchange, vertical transport, and turbulent mixing. However, robust characterization of these processes remains challenging due to sparse observations and uncertainties in numerical models, particularly in dynamically active regions. This study develops a deep learning-based subsurface current reconstruction (DLSCR) model for the Indo-Pacific Convergence Zone (IPCZ), a dynamically complex region characterized by multiscale circulation. The model reconstructs eddy-resolving (1/12°) 3-D subsurface currents down to 643 m from sea surface information—including sea surface currents, height, temperature, salinity, and wind stress. DLSCR demonstrates robust reconstruction skill throughout the upper 400 m, with low root-mean-square errors and high spatiotemporal correlations. This capability is further illustrated by the model's representation of key upper ocean dynamical features in the IPCZ, including the spatiotemporal evolution of subsurface mesoscale eddies and the 3-D structure of the subtropical gyre. Beyond reconstruction skill, a perturbation-based interpretability analysis identifies surface currents (U/V) and sea surface height (SSH) as the inputs to which DLSCR is most sensitive. Sensitivity to surface currents is strongest in the mixed layer (0–50 m), whereas sensitivity to SSH is more pronounced in the thermocline (50–150 m). These results demonstrate that DLSCR provides an accurate and physically interpretable framework for reconstructing the eddying ocean interior.
author: Qin Duan, Xinlong Li, Yuhong Zhang, Yuhang Zheng, Mingyang Wang, Yifan Xia, Wei Wu, Ying Zhang, Qiwei Sun, Lianyi Zhang, Yan Du

title: Multilooking Trade-Offs in Deep-Learning SAR Ship Detection
content: This study examines whether adding multilooking before median filtering in synthetic aperture radar ship detection produces a larger performance deficit at strict than at lenient box-overlap criteria. Four pipelines—single-look intensity (C1), multilooking (C2), median filtering (C3), and multilooking followed by median filtering (C4)—were evaluated with three you only look once (YOLO) architectures and eight random seeds (96 YOLO models) on three scene-disjoint COSMO-SkyMed X-band test acquisitions. Performance was assessed using mean Average Precision (mAP), validation-selected F1, and an intersection-over-union (IoU) sweep from 0.3 to 0.8. At IoU = 0.3, the maximum within-architecture spread was approximately 0.006, and C4’s approximately 0.001 mean advantage over C3 was not significant. At IoU = 0.7, C3 exceeded C4 by 0.144–0.235 mAP across the YOLO architectures; 32 additional real-time detection transformer (RT-DETR ) models showed the same direction. Under a common recall requirement, an offshore evaluation over 1672 km2 showed a small C4 false-alarm benefit for YOLO but the opposite ordering for RT-DETR. Larger box-extent errors with similar center errors provide a geometric interpretation of the strict-IoU penalty, while the factorial comparison shows that multilooking alone can benefit YOLOv8m. These findings challenge adopting the combined preprocessing by default on a speckle-suppression rationale and support selection based on the detector and downstream localization and false-alarm requirements.
author: Sung-Hyun Gong, Hyung-Sup Jung, Lei Zhang

title: RS-ReXSeg: Rejection-Aware Explanatory Language-Guided Segmentation for Open-Query Remote Sensing Images
content: Language-guided remote sensing image segmentation enables pixel-level localization from natural-language queries, but most existing methods implicitly assume that the queried target is present. In open-query interpretation, absent targets and visually similar land-cover objects may cause models to generate incorrect masks, posing risks to disaster assessment, infrastructure monitoring, and urban facility search. To address this issue, we propose RS-ReXSeg, a rejection-aware multimodal large language model framework that jointly performs target segmentation, target-absence rejection, and query-centric explanation. RS-ReXSeg adopts explicit token-level decisions, where [SEG] activates mask decoding for target-present queries and [REJ] suppresses mask generation for target-absent queries. To learn reliable rejection from conventional segmentation annotations, we construct positive, easy-negative, and hard-negative queries, and introduce visual-dominant multivisual–semantic hard-negative query construction with bias-resistant multimode training to improve discrimination under remote-sensing-specific visual confusion. We further construct RS-Rej, a benchmark for jointly evaluating segmentation and rejection. On RS-Rej, RS-ReXSeg achieves 55.6% gIoU and 61.9% cIoU, while achieving 94.1% hard-negative rejection accuracy, compared with 78.5% for GSVA fine-tuned on RS-Rej with random negatives, and maintaining a 99.3% positive-query acceptance rate. On target-present benchmarks, it achieves 73.2% gIoU on EarthReason and 79.58% oIoU on RRSIS-D. Additional evaluation on 75 manually written, scenario-driven free-form queries further assesses robustness to practical query variations. These results indicate that RS-ReXSeg improves target-absence handling while retaining effective target-present segmentation performance.
author: Guangchang Li, Yurong Qian, Chaojun Shi, Yuanxu Wang, Lu Bai, Chen Li

title: MSAWNet: Multiscale Adaptive Interaction and Wavelet Gaussian Attention Method for Hyperspectral Anomaly Detection
content: Hyperspectral anomaly detection (HAD) aims to distinguish anomalies from background under an unsupervised paradigm and has been widely used in various fields. Recently, reconstruction-based deep learning methods have attracted considerable attention in HAD, but they have a limitation that anomalies tend to be incorporated into the reconstructed background. To further suppress the reconstruction of anomaly and accurately reconstruct the background, this article proposes a novel multiscale adaptive interaction and wavelet Gaussian attention method for HAD. Specifically, we design a spatial–spectral adaptive interaction attention module to fuse spatial–spectral information and correctly reconstruct background details, and a wavelet-based Gaussian attention module that suppresses anomaly self-reconstruction by exploiting the difference between high-frequency and low-frequency information to better distinguish anomalies from the background. Furthermore, the overall framework employs multiscale encoding and pyramid decoding to ensure effectiveness in various detection scenarios. Extensive experiments on seven hyperspectral datasets demonstrate the superiority of this method.
author: Jie Xu, Lei Sun, Zixi Yuan, Maohuan Wang, Feng Xie

title: RSIC: Benchmark and Sliding-Window-Based Distortion Correction for Remote Sensing Images
content: Remote sensing images are critical for geoscience research, resource management, and environmental monitoring. However, their usability is often hindered by distortions arising from sensor errors, atmospheric variations, and surface irregularities. The distortion correction of remote sensing images currently depends heavily on labor-intensive manual procedures. While deep learning presents a promising avenue for automation, its application in this specific domain remains largely unexplored. This research gap is primarily attributed to the scarcity of dedicated datasets and standardized evaluation benchmarks. To address this issue, we present the first-ever benchmark dataset specifically designed for remote sensing image distortion and correction, named remote sensing image correction (RSIC). This benchmark includes a diverse collection of distorted images, comprehensive annotations, and challenging scenarios, providing a standardized platform for evaluating correction methods. Furthermore, we propose a novel sliding-window correlation filters (SWCF) method to automatically detect and correct image distortions. The SWCF approach utilizes advanced correlation filtering techniques combined with bidirectional propagation to predict distortion fields with remarkable precision and efficiency. Experimental results demonstrate that SWCF outperforms existing approaches in correction accuracy while providing a controllable tradeoff between accuracy and computational cost through the sliding stride. By introducing the RSIC benchmark and an efficient correction solution, this work addresses critical limitations in remote sensing image analysis and sets the stage for broader applications in cartography, land monitoring, and environmental studies.
author: Hong Zhang, Tingting Huang, Yanda Meng, Yihao Kuang, Jiaqi Wang, Lingyu Jin, Xi Lin, Bo Huang

title: DGCANet: Dynamic Gating Cross-Attention Network With Frequency-Domain Spectral Enhancement for HSI–LiDAR Classification
content: Joint exploitationof hyperspectral image (HSI) and light detection and ranging (LiDAR) data has emerged as a promising approach for land-cover classification. However, existing methods are often limited by the inadequate exploitation of discriminative frequency cues and the presence of unreliable cross-modal interactions. To address these issues, we propose a dynamic gating cross-attention network (DGCANet) with frequency-domain spectral for HSI and LiDAR classification. The architecture adopts a dual-stream parallel framework with frequency-domain enhancement and dynamic-gating interaction. Specifically, a symmetric multiscale attention inception (MSAI) extractor is designed to capture fine-grained spectral–spatial attributes, providing a stable foundation for semantic alignment. Moreover, the FFT-based multiscale feature extractor (FFMS) integrates a frequency modulation branch with a spatial multiscale branch, utilizing a learnable frequency-domain filter to capture global structural features and thereby achieving a unified full-frequency representation of local details and global semantics. To achieve robust cross-modal complementarity, a dynamic gating cross-attention (DGCA) module is designed. It employs a structure-preserving alignment strategy that facilitates bidirectional information exchange while preserving the intrinsic semantic organization of each modality. In particular, it introduces adaptive context-aware gating kernels to dynamically evaluate the credibility of cross-modal features, effectively filtering unreliable responses and suppressing noise propagation. This mechanism significantly enhances feature discriminability and accurately characterizes complex land-cover distributions. Overall, MSAI and FFMS first extract complementary features, which are transformed into semantic tokens and subsequently processed by DGCA for adaptive cross-modal interaction before final classification. Extensive experiments on four public benchmark datasets demonstrate that DGCANet achieves significant improvements over state-of-the-art methods.
author: Ning Jiang, ShengLing Geng, Yuhui Zheng, Le Sun

title: An Unsupervised Hyperspectral Band Selection Method Based on Regional Structure Preservation and Two-Stage Lightweight Greedy Search
content: Hyperspectral band selection is a critical step for reducing data dimensionality, suppressing spectral redundancy, and improving the efficiency of subsequent analysis. Existing unsupervised band selection methods mainly rely on spectral statistical properties and insufficiently exploit the spatial structural information inherent in hyperspectral images, which may limit the discriminability and complementarity of the selected bands. To improve the efficiency of unsupervised band selection, this article proposes a two-stage lightweight greedy band selection (TS-LGBS) method based on regional structure preservation. First, superpixel segmentation is employed to construct a region-level representation, based on which interregion structure preservation and intraregion consistency are established as two complementary reference structures under full-band conditions. Then, each individual band is structurally prescored to construct a high-quality candidate pool. The final band subset is progressively selected from the candidate pool by considering both structural representation capability and interband redundancy, so as to obtain a complementary subset. Experimental results on three public datasets, Indian Pines, Salinas, and Pavia University, demonstrate that compared with several classical and recent unsupervised band selection methods, TS-LGBS achieves competitive classification performance under both SVM and KNN classifiers. The running-time comparison further indicates that shifting complex structural modeling to the prescoring stage can effectively reduce repeated computation during the search process, thereby improving the efficiency of band selection.
author: Lin Hu, Yu Lu, Jiankai Hu, Shu Gan, Xiping Yuan, Tao Guo, Guanglong Li

title: Automated Extraction Techniques for Agricultural Field Boundaries: A Diagnostic Review and Future Framework
content: Accurate delineation of agricultural field boundaries is fundamental to precision agriculture. However, a mismatch between pixel-level segmentation performance and the requirements of object-based agricultural applications still exists even with high-resolution images and advanced models. To clarify the sources of this inconsistency and identify potential solutions, this review employs a hybrid approach combining quantitative scientometric analysis and qualitative comprehensive synthesis. The analysis reveals the research trajectory from traditional gradient features to deep learning, while the qualitative review, which builds on the results of scientometric analysis, examines potential causes within a data-algorithm-evaluation (DAE) framework. Three interconnected issues that lead to the gap between pixel-level segmentation accuracy and object-level agricultural usability requirements are identified. First, a resolution paradox in data acquisition and preprocessing can cause very high resolution imagery to amplify within-field heterogeneity and fine-scale textures, thereby confusing field interiors with true boundaries. Second, a semantic gap in algorithmic modeling limits the ability of deep learning methods to capture the agronomic and management meaning of functional field units. Third, an evaluation disconnection in performance assessment renders conventional pixel-level metrics unsuitable for parcel-based mapping and agricultural applications, favoring high statistical scores despite fragmented or unclosed boundaries. These interconnected issues explain why increased data resolution and model complexity have not consistently improved practical performance. Future advancements should emphasize intelligent data fusion, adaptive foundation models, and topology-oriented evaluation frameworks within the DAE framework. Overall, this review outlines a roadmap for addressing the inconsistency between pixel-oriented evaluation results and object-oriented agricultural applications in agricultural field boundary extraction research.
author: Jinping Gu, Qing Luo, Wenxuan Liu, Zirui Li, Siying Shang, Yang Zhou, Mingxue Zheng

title: DKI-Net: Dynamic Kernel-Interaction Network for Semantic Change Detection in Remote Sensing Images
content: Semantic change detection (SCD) aims to simultaneously locate changed regions and recognize their “from–to” semantic transition types from bitemporal remote sensing images. Recently, Transformer-based architectures have significantly advanced SCD performance by modeling long-range bitemporal dependencies. However, the feedforward network (FFN) in Transformers is input-agnostic, lacks spatial awareness, and lacks explicit modeling of relationships among different response patterns, which may limit the model's ability to capture fine-grained semantic changes in complex remote sensing scenes. To address these issues, we propose DKI-Net, an end-to-end multitask network with a three-branch architecture, whose core component is a kernel-interaction dynamic FFN (KID-FFN). Specifically, KID-FFN consists of three parts. First, a dynamic kernel branch leverages global context to generate input-adaptive $\text{5} \times \text{5}$ spatial filter kernels for each sample and each channel. Second, a static convolution branch combines a bottleneck structure with depthwise convolution to restore local spatial structure. Third, a kernel interaction branch extracts $K$ semantic kernel tokens and performs multihead attention interaction to explicitly model dependencies among different response patterns. In addition, a dual-scale bidirectional change feature enhancement module is introduced to further strengthen change feature representations. Extensive experiments on SECOND and Landsat-SCD demonstrate that DKI-Net achieves superior performance over existing competing methods.
author: Lili Zhang, Weidong Lv, Gaoxu Wang, Rui Shi, Xuejie Zhang

title: Analytical Optimization of Polarimetric Change Detectors for Mapping Open and Grassland Flooding Using Sentinel-1. Case of Rupununi, Guyana
content: Quantifying flood inundation beneath vegetation is critical for understanding flood dynamics in complex wetland environments, where conventional remote sensing approaches often struggle to distinguish between open-water flooding and vegetation-covered inundation. In this study, we propose four novel detectors for the characterization of both open flooding and flooding beneath vegetation using radar-based signal analysis. The methods are developed from two fundamental signal models: the additive model of optimization of power difference and the multiplicative model of optimization of power ratio. Our objective is to investigate additive signal changes can inform or be combined with multiplicative ones. Based on these models, we developed four detectors through different combinations: First, monomial unitary combination, which represents the product of additive and multiplicative models; Second, monomial combination, a parameterized product-based model; Third, linear combination, based on additive integration; Fourth, mixed combination, a data-driven approach. The proposed detectors demonstrated strong potential for quantifying two types of flooding open-water flooding and grassland flooding beneath vegetation with the data-driven detector achieving the best overall performance.
author: Felix Kasiti Isundwa, Armando Marino, Andrea Berardi, C Isabella Bovolo, Peter Hunter, Claire Neil, Thiago S. F. Silva

title: SSF3N: Spectral–Spatial–Frequency Feature Fusion Network for Hyperspectral Marine Oil Spill Detection
content: Marine oil spills pose significant threats to marine ecosystems and coastal economies. Hyperspectral images (HSIs) offer rich spectral–spatial detail to distinguish oil spills from seawater. CNNs capture only local features and overlook spectral nuances, while Transformers falter on high-dimensional, overlapping spectra in oil-spill HSIs. Bandlike spill formations complicate joint spatial–spectral alignment. To address these issues, we propose a novel marine oil spill detection framework by designing a spectral–spatial–frequency feature fusion network (SSF3N) enhanced by the Kolmogorov–Arnold representation theorem. Specifically, this framework presents an improved OTSU-based binary segmentation (IOTSU) to robustly delineate the spatial distribution of oil spills. We then develop a spectral–spatial–frequency feature fusion network, SSF3N, consisting of a hybrid convolutional-KAN (Conv-KAN) module and a FourierKAN attention (FKAT) architecture to capture the nonlinear spectral–spatial–frequency features of oil spills and seawater. The hybrid Conv-KAN component fuses local spectral–spatial cues through convolution and KAN, focusing on fine-grained local and nonlinear spectral–spatial features to distinguish oil from seawater. Meanwhile, FKAT fuses frequency-domain features and extracts global features across the HSIs, targeting both low-frequency spatial structures (e.g., uniform seawater or oil regions) and high-frequency spectral details (e.g., subtle spectral differences between oil and seawater). Experiments on the Hyperspectral Oil Spill Database, consisting of eight scenes, show that our proposed framework outperforms several state-of-the-art detection methods in terms of AUC, Recall, F1-score, and intersection over union, with acceptable computational cost.
author: Yuqing Zhang, Zhijing Ye, Zixuan Xue, Jiangtao Peng, Lefei Zhang

title: MMTNet: A Dual-Branch Multimodal Mutual-Transformer Network for Hyperspectral–LiDAR Land-Cover Classification
content: Multimodal land-cover classification with hyperspectral imagery and light detection and ranging (LiDAR) data remains challenging because of spectral–spatial heterogeneity, modality differences, and limited local discriminability under small-sample supervision. This article proposes a dual-branch multimodal mutual-transformer network (MMTNet) composed of a dual-branch residual encoder (DB-Encoder), a mutual transformer, and a lightweight token-to-pixel (T2P) prediction head (T2P Head). The DB-Encoder extracts modality-specific spectral–spatial and structural features and maps the two branches to compatible token representations of the same dimension. The mutual transformer retains two dense, spatially indexed token streams and performs intramodal self-attention followed by simultaneous HSI-to-LiDAR and LiDAR-to-HSI full-sequence cross-attention. The T2P Head maps the fused local tokens to a spatial logits map and combines the center logits with a fixed local mean using a parameter-free coefficient $\alpha =0.10$. Experiments on Houston2013, Trento, and MUUFL use five fixed data splits and report mean $\pm$ sample standard deviation. MMTNet achieves overall accuracy values of $\text{94.24}\pm \text{2.78}\%$, $\text{99.26}\pm \text{0.24}\%$, and $\text{85.62}\pm \text{1.71}\%$, respectively, demonstrating competitive and stable performance across the three benchmarks. Component, prediction-head, fusion-weight, and architectural sensitivity analyses further clarify the contribution and behavior of the proposed modules. An all-method standardized-input profile shows that MMTNet is performance-oriented rather than lightweight: its parameter and MAC counts are below the two heaviest baselines, while its measured latency lies near the middle of the comparison.
author: Manliang Cao, Xukang Han, Baojiang Li, Xin Chen

title: DPMSNet: Dual-Prior-Guided Multiscale Network for Infrared Small Target Detection
content: Infrared small target detection (IRSTD) has advanced substantially in recent years. Nevertheless, infrared images contain limited discriminative information, as targets exhibit weak texture cues and are easily corrupted by complex backgrounds. As a result, methods that rely solely on visual features are gradually approaching a performance bottleneck. To address this issue, we introduce both language priors and structural priors into IRSTD and propose a dual-prior-guided multiscale network (DPMSNet). Specifically, we design a structural saliency prior module to explicitly characterize local contrast and spatial structure using fixed-parameter operators, thereby enhancing target saliency and suppressing background noise. We further introduce a language prior modulation module, which provides global semantic guidance through structured scene descriptions and requires no textual input during inference. In addition, a progressive multiscale feature extraction module is developed to capture target responses at different scales, and an adaptive scale fusion strategy is adopted to effectively integrate multiscale information. Extensive experiments show that DPMSNet achieves strong overall performance on the NUAA-SIRST, NUDT-SIRST, and IRSTD-1 K datasets, with probability of detection (${P}_{d}$) values of 97.710%, 99.259%, and 94.613%, respectively.
author: Tianci Wang, Feng He, Yichuan Li

title: A Fuzzy-Classification-Based Remote Sensing Approach for Chlorophyll-a Estimation and Spatiotemporal Dynamics Analysis in Chinese Lakes and Reservoirs
content: The optical heterogeneity of inland lake waters poses significant challenges to conventional single-model chlorophyll-a (Chla) estimation approaches. This article developed a fuzzy-classification-based hybrid strategy for Chla estimation. The proposed method adaptively identifies optical water types and optimizes model parameters, thereby overcoming the limitations of single-model approaches and improving estimation accuracy (root mean squared logarithmic error = 0.166; mean absolute percentage error = 31.09%). Using the proposed method and Sentinel-3 OLCI observations acquired from 2016 to 2024, we generated a long-term Chla time-series dataset for 1115 large lakes and reservoirs across China (area > 5 km2). The results indicate an overall decreasing trend in Chla concentrations across national lakes over the past 9 years, suggesting a possible alleviation of eutrophication levels. In terms of intra-annual variability, three typical seasonal patterns were identified at the national scale, including summer trough, continuous decline, and summer peak types. Furthermore, the analysis revealed pronounced regional differences in hydrological, climatic, and ecological characteristics among major lake regions. Coupled analyses of natural and anthropogenic drivers quantified the spatially heterogeneous effects of key variables, including population density, precipitation, cropland proportion, and nighttime light intensity. These analyses further revealed the combined influence of human activities and natural processes on lake ecological conditions. These findings provide an important scientific basis for lake and reservoir management at the national scale.
author: Jinbo An, Fangfang Zhang, Zepeng Wang, Qianqian Wang, Xinyun Li, Shenglei Wang, Junsheng Li

title: Shallow Subsurface Stratigraphy at the Chang’e-6 Landing Site Revealed by Envelope Stacking Imaging of Lunar Regolith Penetrating Radar Data
content: The shallow subsurface structure beneath the Chang’ e-6 landing site on the lunar farside has been inferred mainly from crater morphology and returned sample analyses, whereas the depth and geological nature of the regolith base have not been constrained by in situ radar imaging. Here we apply an envelope stacking method to Lunar Regolith Penetrating Radar data acquired before the Chang’e-6 drilling operation. Replacing coherent summation with envelope summation makes deep imaging less sensitive to the inter-channel phase errors that accumulate with depth for a stationary, limited-aperture array. The imaging results, after correction for the depth-dependent increase in regolith permittivity, reveal a stratified structure within the uppermost approximately 2.2 m beneath the landing site. Three primary units are resolved from top to bottom: a thin near-surface layer interpreted as impact ejecta (0–0.2 m), a relatively homogeneous fine-grained regolith layer (0.2–1.5 m), and a heterogeneous layer containing coarser fragments (1.5–2.2 m). A laterally continuous strong reflection interface at a corrected depth of approximately 2.2 m is interpreted as the base of the regolith and may represent the transition to a denser underlying material, such as a layer rich in coarse rock fragments or the top of the basaltic substrate. This corrected depth is consistent with independent estimates from crater morphology studies, indicating a regolith cover markedly thinner than at previously studied lunar landing sites. The implied time-averaged accumulation rate of $\sim$0.8 m/Gyr is among the lowest of in situ characterized lunar sites, and the stratigraphy places the scooped and drilled CE-6 samples in distinct stratigraphic units, providing a framework for interpreting analyses of the returned samples.
author: Waikei Ng, Yi Xu, Renrui Liu, Rui Chen, Ling Zhang, Di Liang, Wenzhen Lu, Rui Gao

title: A Hybrid Feature Interaction Framework for Bitemporal Change Detection in Complex Environments
content: Accurate change detection (CD) in remote sensing images, particularly in complex environments, such as plateaus and deserts, poses significant challenges due to diverse building sizes, shapes, and environmental conditions. This article proposes a novel hybrid feature interaction framework (HFIF) designed to address these challenges by leveraging cross-temporal, cross-scale, and cross-level feature interaction mechanisms. The framework integrates feature refinement both prior to and after feature differencing, enabling a more comprehensive extraction of spatial and contextual information. A pyramid split attention-based module enhances the focus on crucial channels by capturing local and global dependencies in bitemporal features. The cross-temporal feature interaction module facilitates interimage feature fusion, improving the network's ability to distinguish meaningful changes. Furthermore, the cross-scale attention-based transformer and cross-layer pyramid transformer refine the feature difference maps, addressing scale variation and boundary detection issues. Extensive experiments on four benchmark datasets, including the proposed PD-CD dataset, demonstrate that HFIF outperforms state-of-the-art CD methods, achieving an F1-score and intersection over union of 90.62 and 82.85 on the PD-CD dataset, respectively. These results highlight the framework's effectiveness in detecting building changes under challenging environmental conditions.
author: Xinyu Zhang, Ming He, Haihua Chen, Yanzhi Zhao, Boxiong Hu

title: Refinement of OLCI Water Vapor Retrieval Using GNSS Observations by Transformer Network in Chinese Mainland
content: Atmospheric water vapor monitoring based on satellite observations has significantly contributed to achieving wide-area monitoring for global applications. However, the performance of water vapor from satellite observations is vulnerable to multiple factors under different conditions, making a significant potential for accuracy improvement. In this regard, a refined retrieving model based on the original observations of Ocean and Land Colour Imager (OLCI) and precipitable water vapor (PWV) from Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) was established. The empirical linear relationship between PWV and OLCI radiance observations were firstly applied for retrieval. Results showed that the root-mean-square errors (RMSE) between the model outputs and references from GNSS and ERA5 reanalysis were 3.8 mm and 4.2 mm, respectively. Afterward, three neural network architectures—LSTM, CNN, and Transformer—were implemented for better accuracy. Among them, the Transformer model achieved the best performance, with an RMSE of 2.51 mm relative to GNSS-PWV, representing a 48% improvement over the OLCI Level-2 product. Finally, atmospheric pressure and weighted mean temperature were incorporated in model refinement, which further improved the accuracy of model outputs to 1.9 mm. In general, this proposed method can greatly improve the accuracy of water vapor retrieval for OLCI, which is beneficial for meteorological and hydrological applications in Chinese mainland.
author: Lei Fan, Yibing Liu, Linghao Zhou, Chuang Shi, James Chakwizira

title: Neutrosophic Uncertainty-Parameterized Mamba for Hyperspectral Image Classification
content: Hyperspectral image classification must model long-range spectral structure while handling mixed pixels and uncertain class boundaries. Existing selective state-space classifiers use input-dependent parameters, and explicit local reliability information can guide their parameter generators. We introduce NUP-Mamba, which derives neutrosophic-inspired truth and indeterminacy descriptors, together with complementary falsity, from spectral tokens for selective-parameter generation. These descriptors condition the input-injection term $B$, discretization step $\Delta$, and output gate of a bidirectional Mamba encoder, while the transition matrix $A$ remains stable and input independent. Local reliability thereby controls how evidence enters and leaves the recurrence while preserving its transition dynamics. Matched controls and a capacity stress test on HanChuan support this descriptor-to-parameter pathway. Cross-dataset evaluations show that the benefit depends on the scene and module configuration. Uncertainty maps and parameter diagnostics associate high indeterminacy with elevated error risk and changes in generated $B$ and $\Delta$. The results support uncertainty-conditioned parameter generation as a complementary mechanism for spectral–spatial state-space classifiers.
author: Xueliang Wang, Ping Wu

title: Geo-AIRL: A Geospatial Correlation-Guided Adaptive Iterative Refinement Localization Framework for Visual Geo-Localization
content: Visual geo-localization (VG) enables autonomous uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAV) positioning by matching aerial images to satellite maps without external signals. However, conventional coarse-to-fine two-stage pipelines suffer from a substantial efficiency bottleneck. This limitation stems from treating the satellite reference database as an unordered image collection, which forces coarse retrieval to undertake fine-grained discrimination beyond its intrinsic capability while confining precise localization to the candidate space predefined by the coarse stage. To address this issue, we propose Geo-AIRL, a geospatial correlation-guided adaptive iterative refinement localization framework for UAV visual geo-localization. In the offline stage, geospatial correlation modeling organizes the reference database into a geographically ordered structure and establishes a unified global coordinate system, providing an explicit spatial foundation for subsequent localization.
