In the online stage, local response candidate screening performs region-level coarse localization over the ordered reference space and yields a compact set of spatially reliable candidates. Starting from these candidates, spatial mapping-driven adaptive iterative refinement progressively improves localization precision through adaptive closed-loop refinement in the global coordinate space. In addition, the covisible region similarity metric is introduced for final result determination. Experiments on the ALTO and NewYorkFly datasets demonstrate superior localization performance and efficiency advantages over conventional two-stage baselines.
author: Chenji Wang, Xiang Zhang, Yanzi Shi, Wenjun Huang, Pengchao He, Hangzai Luo, Sheng Zhong

title: Evaluation of LAI Retrieval Bias for Coniferous and Broad-Leaved Mixed Forests Using a Stochastic-Radiative-Transfer-Based Algorithm
content: Leaf area index (LAI) retrieval is fundamental for large-scale monitoring of forest growth, evolution, and health. The current LAI retrieval algorithms mainly differentiate between coniferous forests and broad-leaved forests, while the increasing coverage of coniferous and broad-leaved mixed forests worldwide has brought about more sources of bias in the forest LAI products. It is difficult but significant for the classical LAI inversion algorithm to address the complex spatial heterogeneity of mixed forests. In this article, a coniferous and broad-leaved mixed forest dataset was established for evaluation experiments, consisting of 3750 simulated mixed-forest plots with specific structures generated by the three-dimensional radiative transfer model LESS, 21 field-measured mixed forest plots, and 76 mixed forest plots collected from the National Ecological Observatory Network dataset. The stochastic radiative transfer (SRT) model used in moderate resolution imaging spectroradiometer LAI products was utilized to evaluate the LAI retrieval bias in the application of coniferous and broad-leaved mixed forests. A lookup table (LUT) approach integrating both conifer and broadleaf species was proposed to improve LAI retrieval performance in mixed forests. Compared with the conventional broadleaf and coniferous LUTs, the integrated LUT demonstrated moderately improved applicability in both simulated mixed-forest plots (R2integrated = 0.905, R2broadleaf = 0.894, R2coniferous = 0.731; RMSEintegrated = 0.128 m2·m−2, RMSEbroadleaf = 0.132 m2·m−2, RMSEconiferous = 0.074 m2·m−2; RIintegrated = 100.0%, RIbroadleaf = 96.8%, RIconiferous = 35.0%) and field mixed-forest plots (R2integrated = 0.511, R2broadleaf = 0.434, R2coniferous = 0.333; RMSEintegrated = 1.652 m2·m−2, RMSEbroadleaf = 1.733 m2·m−2, RMSEconiferous = 1.106 m2·m−2; RIintegrated = 80.4%, RIbroadleaf = 72.2%, RIconiferous = 22.7%). The simulation experiments revealed that the effect of mixing ratio, tree density, and vertical distribution of tree species on LAI retrieval in mixed forests indicated regular biases controlled by the characteristics of coniferous and broad-leaved tree species. The bias mechanisms were further explained in field sample plots by an attribution analysis based on random forest and SHapley Additive exPlanations. This article systematically evaluates the bias of the LAI retrieval algorithm based on the SRT model in coniferous and broad-leaved mixed forests, which provides theoretical support for the improvement of the LAI retrieval algorithm for coniferous and broad-leaved mixed forests and more accurate monitoring of complex forest surface information.
author: Yuxuan Liu, Xiaoyao Li, Huaguo Huang, Xuexia Sun, Zhuangzhuang Zhang

title: RWKVHSI: Dual-Stream Recurrent Spectral–Spatial Evidence Fusion for Efficient Hyperspectral Image Classification
content: Hyperspectral image (HSI) classification requires reconciling highly correlated spectral responses with spatially heterogeneous structures while controlling computational cost. Convolutional networks provide strong local inductive biases but capture long-range context only indirectly, whereas self-attention improves global interaction at quadratic token cost. In this article, we introduce RWKVHSI, a compact dual-stream recurrent framework that models complementary pointwise channel-transformed and spatial-structural evidence. A shared stem first embeds each HSI patch. The pointwise channel-transformation stream operates independently at each spatial location, while the spatial-structural stream extracts local neighborhood patterns through lightweight convolution. Both representations are serialized row-wise and processed by independently parameterized recurrent weighted key–value blocks whose state updates are linear in sequence length and avoid pairwise attention maps. An adaptive channel-fusion module derives global branch descriptors, recalibrates their responses, and integrates them through residual learning. Experiments on Indian Pines, Houston2013, and WHU-Hi-LongKou show that RWKVHSI achieves competitive or superior accuracy relative to representative convolutional, transformer, and state-space baselines while maintaining a compact computational footprint. Ablation and sensitivity analyzes further verify the complementary contributions of the two streams, adaptive fusion, recurrent depth, and residual optimization. These results demonstrate an effective accuracy–efficiency tradeoff for within-scene HSI classification through recurrent spectral–spatial evidence decomposition.
author: Xiaofei Yang, Xiaolin Luo, Zihang Luo, Ying Liu, Yuanchao Su

title: TCMA: Text-Conditioned Multigranularity Alignment for Drone Cross-Modal Text–Video Retrieval
content: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) have emerged as powerful platforms for real-time, high-resolution data collection, generating large quantities of aerial videos. Efficient text–video retrieval is crucial for applications including urban management, emergency response, security, and disaster relief. Research on UAV-based retrieval remains underexplored, as existing datasets suffer from coarse-grained and redundant captions. In this work, we construct a fine-grained drone video–text match dataset (DVTMD), consisting of 2864 videos and 14 320 semantically diverse captions. To foster this task, we propose the text-conditioned multi-granularity alignment (TCMA) framework, which integrates global video-sentence alignment, sentence-guided frame aggregation, and word-guided patch alignment. To further refine local alignment, we design a word and patch selection module that filters irrelevant content, as well as a text-adaptive dynamic temperature mechanism that adapts attention sharpness to text type. Extensive experiments on DVTMD and CapERA establish the comprehensive benchmark for drone text–video retrieval. Our TCMA achieves state-of-the-art results, with R@1 scores of 45.5% for text-to-video retrieval and 42.8% for video-to-text retrieval. The complete codebase and dataset will be available.
author: Zixu Zhao, Yang Zhan, Yunhao Li, Yan Li

title: CBAM-ResNet for Raw-I/Q-Based Multisource DOA Estimation With Off-Grid Spectral Decoding
content: Direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation in array signal-processing systems remains challenging under low signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs). Sample covariance matrix (SCM)-based deep learning methods can improve statistical stability through temporal averaging, but this preprocessing may also suppress snapshot-level phase cues that are useful for high-resolution estimation. To address this tradeoff, this article proposes convolutional block attention module (CBAM)-ResNet, a raw in-phase/quadrature (I/Q)-based DOA estimation framework that combines residual feature extraction with channel-spatial attention. The proposed network maps raw I/Q snapshots to a multilabel spatial spectrum, while the embedded CBAM reweights noise-dominated feature responses in the learned sensor-time representation. To support the snapshot-number range evaluated in this study, temporal pooling is used to aggregate snapshot-dependent features without changing the network architecture. In addition, a non-maximum suppression (NMS)-guided parabolic interpolation decoder refines discrete spectral peaks and reduces off-grid quantization errors. Simulations with an 8-element uniform linear array (ULA) evaluate the proposed method under two-source and seven-source settings. Specifically, the two-source evaluations use $T=512$ for the SNR and random off-grid tests, vary $T$ in the snapshot-number test, and impose a minimum source separation of $4^\circ$ in the random-angle test. The conclusions concerning snapshot-number variation and random off-grid estimation are therefore restricted to these evaluated ranges. Quantitatively, in the dual-source setting, CBAM-ResNet achieves a root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 0.178 deg with a Hit@1 deg rate of 100%, reducing the RMSE by 23.6% compared with IQ-ResNet and remaining comparable to invariance techniques (ESPRIT), which obtains 0.184 deg. In the seven-source stress test CBAM-ResNet obtains an RMSE of 0.287 deg with a Hit@1 deg rate of 98.99%. These results are achieved with only a 2.4% parameter increase over IQ-ResNet, suggesting that attention-stabilized raw-I/Q learning improves accuracy and multisource stability under the tested simulated ULA conditions.
author: Yaokun Wu, Kun Ye, Chuanxi Xing, Lang Zhou, Haixin Sun

title: Time-Domain P-Wave Impedance Inversion Using a Learning-Based Approach: A Sleipner CO2 Monitoring Study
content: Time-lapse (4D) seismic monitoring is widely used for tracking subsurface changes associated with CO2 storage; however, conventional inversion approaches often suffer from nonuniqueness related to baseline velocity models and time–depth conversion, while data-driven approaches typically require large volumes of training data generated through computationally intensive numerical modeling. This study presents a time-domain P-wave impedance inversion framework using a learning-based approach that directly estimates impedance changes from near-offset seismic data. The method is trained on physics-based synthetic datasets generated from Marmousi2-derived models incorporating rock-physics–guided CO2 plume simulations and forward seismic modeling. A trace-based learning strategy is adopted to predict impedance-change profiles, enabling efficient processing and robust generalization to field data while preserving sensitivity to thin-layer effects. Application to the Sleipner dataset demonstrates that the proposed method produces laterally coherent plume footprints and vertically stacked, thin-layered impedance-reduction features consistent with established geological interpretations. Additional comparisons with seismic differences and preprocessing variations confirm that the inversion results are physically consistent and robust. These results indicate that the proposed framework provides a reliable approach for time-lapse CO2 monitoring, particularly for detecting and tracking plume evolution.
author: Sooyoon Kim, Junyon Park, Soon Jee Seol, Joongmoo Byun

title: BCG-Former: Toward Pareto-Efficient Hyperspectral Image Classification via Band-Contextual Gating
content: Hyperspectral image (HSI) classification systems are increasingly deployed on platforms with strict computational budgets, such as UAVs and small spaceborne sensors. In these settings, accuracy alone is not enough; the model must also run within tight latency and memory constraints. Most recent HSI classifiers, however, focus on accuracy and pay relatively little attention to these constraints. We propose BCG-Former, a lightweight convolutional neural network (CNN)–Transformer hybrid that targets this tradeoff. The model introduces three innovations: band-contextual gating (BCG) for adaptive spectral recalibration using local interchannel context and learnable temperature sharpening, a spectral summary token that bridges spectral and spatial features, and single-pass Band-RoPE combined with linear attention for efficient joint representation learning. Evaluated on classical airborne (Pavia University, Salinas, Indian Pines, Houston 2013/2018) and UAV-borne benchmark datasets (WHU-Hi-LongKou, HongHu, and HanChuan), BCG-Former achieves state-of-the-art or competitive accuracies while maintaining submillisecond inference latency (0.81–0.94 ms/image) and using only 0.10–0.23 M parameters. Across all eight benchmarks, BCG-Former consistently resides on or near the Pareto frontier of accuracy versus latency, outperforming or matching recent CNN-, Transformer-, and Mamba-based methods at a fraction of their computational cost. Ablation studies confirm that the components are complementary, with both BCG and linear attention making substantial contributions to the overall accuracy-efficiency tradeoff. These results establish BCG-Former as a strong accuracy-efficiency Pareto candidate for real-time and large-scale remote sensing applications.
author: Gaurav Sharma, Eungjoo Lee

title: A Flexible Plug-and-Play Framework With Scene-Specific Priors for TomoSAR Reconstruction
content: Tomographic synthetic aperture radar (TomoSAR) is an advanced remote sensing technology for retrieving high-resolution 3-D information of observed scenes. Existing TomoSAR reconstruction methods have widely employed explicit regularizers, such as the $L_{1}$-norm and total variation, to improve tomographic reconstruction quality. However, explicit regularizers are typically tied to specific scattering assumptions, making a single regularizer insufficient for scenes where, for example, sparse scattering from urban structures and continuous volumetric scattering from forests coexist. The plug-and-play (PnP) framework offers a promising solution by decoupling the prior model from the physical forward model, thereby allowing different priors to be flexibly substituted without modifying the iterative framework. More importantly, PnP can accommodate nonanalytical priors, such as deep neural networks, which can learn complex scattering features that are difficult to describe using explicit regularizers. To exploit this flexibility for TomoSAR reconstruction involving different scattering mechanisms, this article proposes a flexible 3-D tomographic reconstruction framework based on PnP priors and the fast iterative shrinkage-thresholding algorithm. A common data-fidelity formulation is used for different scene types, while scene-dependent prior knowledge is introduced through interchangeable PnP plugins. Specifically, two tailored nonanalytical priors are employed, with a fully convolutional autoencoder used for urban building areas and a U-Net used for forest areas. Experiments with both simulated and real data demonstrate that the proposed strategy improves TomoSAR reconstruction by exploiting the advantages of scene-specific PnP priors.
author: Kun Wang, Yizhe Fan, Jie Li, Zhe Zhang, Bingchen Zhang, Yirong Wu

title: Hyperspectral Image Small Target Detection: A Taylor-Type Six-Point Adaptive Discrete Neural Dynamics Approach
content: In complex background scenarios, hyperspectral image small target detection (HISTD) is crucial for fine-grained information extraction and resource localization. However, existing traditional detection algorithms are simple, resulting in a high miss rate for weak targets. In contrast, data-driven methods suffer from poor generalization due to annotation difficulty and data scarcity. In this context, constrained energy minimization (CEM), which requires no annotations and can suppress background interference while enhancing target responses, has become a mainstream method. However, its solution process involves large-scale high-dimensional matrix operations, leading to slow convergence and low accuracy. To address this issue, this article proposes an HISTD method based on a Taylor-type six-point adaptive discrete neural dynamics CEM model (T6ADND-CEM). The method is built on the zeroing neural dynamics framework. An adaptive coefficient is introduced to accelerate convergence, and a Taylor-type six-point discrete formula is used for implementation. In addition, an adaptive step size is incorporated to further improve solution accuracy. Experimental results show that T6ADND-CEM achieves good accuracy and fast convergence in HISTD tasks, with a steady-state error of $\text{5.9281} \times \text{10}^{-\text{14}}$ and a convergence time of 0.2320 s. Compared with other methods, the proposed method shows better error control and convergence efficiency, while requiring no large-scale labeled training data.
author: Jiayi Feng, Jieming Liang, Jiayan Chen, Cong Lin, Zhong Xue

title: Robust Forest Road Distress Detection in Complex UAV Remote Sensing Scenes via Wavelet Enhancement and Dual Contrastive Learning
content: Accurate and timely forest road distress detection is essential for effective forest infrastructure management. However, UAV-based monitoring of forest roads remains challenging due to complex backgrounds, occlusions, and pseudodistress patterns. To address these issues, this study proposes a wavelet-enhanced dual contrastive learning network (WDCLNet) for forest road distress detection using UAV remote sensing imagery. A WavePoint convolution module is first developed by integrating wavelet-based multiscale feature extraction with pointwise feature aggregation, enabling the network to capture fine-grained distress characteristics under complex imaging conditions. Based on this module, a wavelet multiscale feature extractor is constructed to improve the representation of distress patterns with different scales and structures. Furthermore, a prototype-anchored bidirectional contrastive learning strategy is introduced to enhance the discrimination between real distress and twig pseudodistress. The proposed strategy jointly optimizes intraclass compactness and interclass separability by leveraging class prototypes as semantic anchors. To evaluate the proposed method, a UAV-based Forest Road MultiDistress Detection dataset (UAV-FRDD) is constructed, containing diverse distress categories and complex forest road scenarios. Extensive experiments on the proposed dataset and public benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of WDCLNet. On the UAV-FRDD dataset, WDCLNet achieves 81.5% Precision, 76.2% Recall, and 82.1% mAP@0.5, outperforming the strongest baseline, RT-DETR, by 5.3%, 3.6%, and 5.5%, respectively. Under the road-section-independent evaluation protocol, WDCLNet retains its advantage over RT-DETR across mAP@0.5 and stricter metrics. These results indicate its potential for UAV-based intelligent forest road inspection.
author: Lin Zhao, Xinmin Tao, Yanping Zhang

title: Separating Spectral-Response and Residual Radiometric Biases in Microwave Sounder SNO Intercomparisons: Early On-Orbit Assessment of FY-3H/MWTS-3
content: Observed simultaneous nadir overpass (SNO) differences between nonidentical microwave sounders combine residual radiometric inconsistencies with scene-dependent spectral-response-function (SRF) mismatch, but these contributions are often evaluated together. Although SRFs affect simulated radiances and data assimilation, their contribution is rarely isolated from residual radiometric differences in observed intersensor SNO comparisons. A paired-SRF framework is developed for the early on-orbit assessment of the microwave temperature sounder-3 (MWTS-3) onboard FengYun-3H against NOAA-21/advanced technology microwave sounder (ATMS). Paired RTTOV simulations use identical atmospheric, surface, and viewing-geometry inputs with the respective official MWTS-3 and ATMS coefficients. Near-nadir field-of-view selection reduces polarization effects when estimating the SRF contribution. Cumulative statistical stability analysis, surface-response diagnostics, and distribution-shape tests define channel- and scene-specific applicability domains before transferring estimated SRF contributions to observations. On a 30% held-out simulation set, the correction reduces mean absolute error by 29.3%–83.2% for Channels 1–5 and 7 over Arctic ocean and by 24.5%–86.3% for Channels 9–17 over all valid Arctic surfaces relative to the no-SRF-correction baseline. In Arctic SNO comparisons, the Channel-9 mean difference changes from $-$0.70 to $-$ 0.28 K, and the corrected absolute mean differences for Channels 9–17 remain within approximately 0.33 K. The correction also exposes error cancellation: the Channel-3 difference changes from $-$0.41 to $-$1.47 K after the SRF term is removed. Thus, the framework converts instrument SRF knowledge into an explicit bias-attribution step rather than treating the observed SNO difference as a single calibration term, and provides an early quantitative benchmark for FY-3H/MWTS-3.
author: Shi Liu, Juyang Hu, Na Xu, Jian Shang, Xiuqing Hu, Yang Guo

title: High-Resolution Time-Reassigned Synchrosqueezing Transform and Its Application
content: The conventional time–frequency domain time-delay-based time-reassigned synchrosqueezing transform can greatly enhance the time–frequency resolution. However, it neither considers the impacts of background noise beyond the effective frequency band of the input signal on time–frequency spectrum generation, time–frequency domain time-delay (TFTD) estimation and time-reassigned synchrosqueezing, nor removes (or minimizes) the impacts of the time–frequency phase (the time–frequency domain phase) period-jump and frequency-sampling interval on TFTD estimation, limiting its further application. In order to eliminate (or minimize) the impacts of these issues during the time-reassigned synchrosqueezing, thereby achieving high-resolution high-SNR (signal-to-noise ratio) time-reassigned synchrosqueezing results, we propose a high-resolution time-reassigned synchrosqueezing transform (HTRST). HTRST main contains the flowchart of HTRST, the effective frequency band constrained input signal frequency spectrum SNR enhancement (EFSE), the continuous time–frequency phase-based high-precision time–frequency domain time-delay estimation (CHTE), and the high-precision time–frequency domain time-delay-based high-resolution time-reassigned synchrosqueezing (HHTS). EFSE aims to utilize effective frequency band (or dynamic range) analysis to the frequency spectrum of the input signal for denoising, thereby eliminating the impact of background noise beyond the effective frequency band of the input signal, ultimately obtaining the input signal high-SNR frequency spectrum for high-SNR time–frequency spectrum generation. CHTE aims to first form the continuous time–frequency phase of the generated high-SNR time–frequency spectrum to remove the impact of the time–frequency phase period-jump, and then perform the differentiation operation to the continuous time–frequency phase to minimize the impact of frequency-sampling interval, thereby obtaining the high-precision time–frequency domain time-delay (HTFTD) for HHTS. HHTS aims to use the HTFTD obtained by CHTE for iterative high-resolution time-reassigned synchrosqueezing, thereby obtaining high-resolution time-reassigned synchrosqueezing results. Theoretical analysis on a synthetic 1-D seismic signal and the application on a field 3-Dseismic dataset demonstrate that HTRST obtains high-resolution time-reassigned synchrosqueezing results and can be used in digital signal processing and interpretation.
author: Chenxi Liang, Gulan Zhang, Xiangwen Li, Qihong Zhong, Yiliang Luo, Shirui Liu, Suhai Chen, Zili Tang

title: Spatiotemporal Distribution Analysis and Quality Validation for TianMu-1 GNOS-M Radio Occultation Atmospheric Profiles
content: The spatiotemporal coverage and quality of GNSS radio occultation (GNSS RO) data are critical for numerical weather prediction and climate studies. The Chinese TianMu-1 (TM-1) commercial small-satellite meteorological constellation, consisting of 23 satellites equipped with the miniaturized GNSS Occultation Sounder (GNOS-M), provides a large number of GNSS RO observations. This study systematically evaluated the spatiotemporal distribution and data quality of TM-1 GNOS-M atmospheric products, which were cross-validated against FengYun-3 (FY-3) GNOS II and COSMIC-2 using observational data from May 2025. The results showed that the 22-satellite TM-1 operational constellation delivered around 25 000 globally distributed atmospheric profiles daily and achieved near-global coverage within 24 h via multi-GNSS observations, with a global coverage fraction of 98.7% on the 5°×5° defined grid—marking a significant improvement compared with traditional single-satellite and six-satellite RO missions. Further comparisons with FY-3 GNOS II and COSMIC-2 revealed that constellation configuration significantly affected latitude–local time coverage, where TM-1 exhibited distinct advantages in mid-latitude and polar regions. Regarding the data quality, comparisons with European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts fifth-generation reanalysis data (ERA5) over the 5–35 km range showed that TM-1 GNOS-M bending angle and refractivity mean bias remained small, with standard deviation generally below 6% and 2%, respectively. Over the 200–1000 hPa layer, the 3CH-derived error variances (percentage squared) for refractivity and temperature were generally confined to within 1.1%2 and 0.1%2, respectively. These findings demonstrated that TM-1 GNOS-M atmospheric data quality was broadly comparable to those of FY-3 GNOS II and COSMIC-2.
author: Congliang Liu, Jiahui Liang, Yueqiang Sun, Xianyi Wang, Weihua Bai, Xiangguang Meng, Peng Hu, Guangyuan Tan, Cong Yin, Ruhan Wu, Yuerong Cai, Wei Li, Feixiong Huang

title: M2-DINO: Parameter-Efficient and Topology-Oriented Multimodal Fusion for Remote Sensing Image Segmentation
content: Vision foundation models (VFMs) provide strong transferable visual representations for remote sensing image segmentation. However, adapting these models to multimodal remote sensing data remains challenging because of heterogeneous modality gaps, cross-modal feature imbalance, and the attenuation of fine-grained structural details in deep representations. To address these issues, we propose M2-DINO, a parameter-efficient multimodal adaptation framework for remote sensing semantic segmentation. M2-DINO keeps most pretrained weights of a SAT-493M-pretrained distilled DINOv3 vision transformer-large/16 (ViT-L/16) backbone fixed and introduces three trainable components at different network stages. First, a heterogeneous multimodal mixture-of-experts (H-M3E) adapter is inserted into selected ViT residual streams to perform token-level heterogeneous adaptation over optical, auxiliary, and spatial expert responses. Second, a gated lateral module recalibrates lateral and top-down features in the decoder pyramid through spatial gates to reduce potential feature imbalance. Third, a topology-oriented auxiliary skip connection (TASC) injects gated stride-4 auxiliary structural cues into the high-resolution decoder level. In this work, the topology-oriented terminology refers to architectural sensitivity to topology-relevant structures, such as thin-object continuity and object boundaries, rather than explicit optimization of topological invariants. Experiments on the WHU-OPT-SAR, YESeg-OPT-SAR, and DW9c datasets show competitive segmentation accuracy, reaching mean intersection over union scores of 57.50%, 69.19%, and 67.12%, respectively, while optimizing only a subset of the overall model parameters.
author: Zifei Luo, Yubi He, Zhiyong Li, Zhiqiang Li, Lingyuan Zhao, Bo Yang, Keqiang Xu

title: WaveUIE: Efficient Wavelet-Domain Underwater Image Enhancement
content: Underwater image enhancement (UIE) remains challenging because underwater degradations are not uniform in the image space: color distortion and illumination attenuation mainly affect global appearance, while scattering and blurring largely degrade local textures and structural details. However, most existing deep UIE methods formulate enhancement as a generic spatial-domain restoration problem, leaving the frequency-dependent nature of underwater degradations insufficiently explored. In this article, we revisit UIE from a wavelet-domain perspective and identify a degradation-frequency correspondence: low-frequency components are closely related to global color and illumination correction, whereas high-frequency components are more responsible for texture and detail restoration. Based on this observation, we propose WaveUIE, a degradation-aware wavelet-domain enhancement framework that explicitly decomposes underwater images into low- and high-frequency components and restores them with targeted modeling. Rather than treating different frequency components independently, WaveUIE further introduces low-frequency-guided high-frequency refinement to achieve coherent restoration between global appearance and local details. Moreover, we exploit degraded underwater images not merely as inputs but also as informative negative samples, and propose a wavelet fine-grained contrastive policy to learn discriminative degradation-aware representations across multiple wavelet sub-bands. Extensive experiments on UIEB, large-scale underwater image, and enhancement of underwater visual perception demonstrate that WaveUIE achieves state-of-the-art performance in both full-reference and no-reference metrics, while maintaining a favorable accuracy-efficiency tradeoff.
author: Yiyuan Ge, Zhihao Chen, Ziyang Wang

title: Video SAR Target Tracking via Shadow-Guided Re-Association and Occlusion Recovery
content: Shadow-guided video synthetic aperture radar (video SAR) shadow target tracking has become a mainstream research direction in this field because it is unaffected by target reflection characteristics and motion velocity. Current video SAR shadow target tracking faces three core challenges: trajectory breakage due to occlusion, prediction bias caused by nonlinear motion, and frequent identity switching due to highly similar shadow appearances. To address these challenges, this article proposes a tracking method via shadow-guided re-association and occlusion recovery. First, we design a shadow center interpolation module to reconstruct the state during shadow occlusion. Second, we design a shadow center momentum module to improve velocity correction under nonlinear motion of shadow targets. Finally, we design a shadow center reupdate module to implement a reassociation mechanism after long shadow occlusion, reducing identity switching. Experiments on the SNL public video SAR dataset show that our method achieves a MOTA of 85.50%, an IDF1 of 90.60%, and an identity switch of only seven times. Its overall performance significantly outperforms mainstream trackers such as SORT and DeepSORT, as well as advanced methods based on graph neural networks and reidentification features, verifying the tracking effectiveness of the proposed framework in weak-feature and high-noise scenarios and providing a viable technical approach for video SAR target tracking.
author: Xueqi Wu, Zhongzhen Sun, Han Wu, Kefeng Ji

title: A Spatiotemporal Coenhancement Network for Satellite Video Super-Resolution
content: In recent years, satellite video has emerged as a pivotal Earth observation technology, attracting considerable attention for its capability to capture dynamic information. Despite its growing importance, most existing studies focus on enhancing the spatial resolution of satellite videos, while research on joint spatiotemporal super-resolution remains extremely limited. Spatiotemporal coenhancement not only facilitates the reconstruction of clearer videos but also effectively captures the dynamic changes of surface features, thereby providing more accurate data support for monitoring and analyzing complex spatiotemporal changes. Therefore, a spatiotemporal coenhancement network is proposed for satellite video super-resolution. First, we propose a spatiotemporal mamba module to construct an efficient interframe modeling mechanism. This module integrates the vision state space module, dual scale convolutional attention, and multiscale feature fusion blocks in a multistage fusion scheme. By combining their complementary strengths in long-range dependence modeling, multiscale perception, and feature fusion, it accurately generates intermediate frame representations. Second, we propose a bidirectional temporal difference modulation module . Through bidirectional propagation and differential computation, it adaptively enhances cross-frame features and aggregates global spatiotemporal context, ultimately improving the reconstruction quality. Extensive experiments on satellite video datasets demonstrate that our method outperforms current state-of-the-art approaches in both qualitative and quantitative evaluations.
author: Hongliang Chang, Haijiang Sun, Qiaoyuan Liu, Xiaowen Zhang

title: DQE$^{2}$-ST: A Topology-Aware Dynamic Quadtree and Edge-Enhanced Swin Transformer for Remote Sensing Scene Classification
content: Remote sensing scene classification (RSSC) is a core task in remote sensing image analysis. A robust RSSC model should adapt local modeling granularity to diverse scenes while preserving the structural integrity of ground objects, and in particular delivering unbroken representations for elongated ground objects. However, existing methods often suffer from geospatial topological disruption and the loss of high-frequency fine-grained features. To address this problem, this article proposes a topology-aware dynamic quadtree and edge-enhanced Swin transformer, named DQE$^{2}$-ST (where DQ stands for dynamic quadtree and E$^{2}$ represents edge-enhanced). The proposed framework contains two coupled modules. The dynamic quadtree attention (DQA) module adaptively adjusts modeling granularity through topology-aware split-line planning. It can automatically bypass compact objects while maintaining their semantic integrity. However, it inevitably disrupts the topological continuity of elongated ground objects across windows. The high-low frequency decoupled edge enhancer (HLF-EE) module is capable of extracting topology-aware high-frequency prior information and integrating it across different scales. Through edge enhancement, it repairs the continuity loss, thereby effectively achieving the semantic fusion of these linear features. Experiments on aerial image dataset, NWPU-RESISC45, UC Merced Land Use, and WHU-RS19 verify the effectiveness of DQE$^{2}$-ST. The proposed method achieves 96.38% overall accuracy on NWPU-RESISC45 under the 20% training split. Further analyses confirm that the advantages of the DQA and HLF-EE modules in balancing classification accuracy, topological preservation, and computational efficiency, requiring only 3.79–3.86 G floating-point operations across all evaluation settings.
author: Lei Zhang, Qian Wang, Changfeng Jing, Xing Xing, Chengwei Yang

title: Re-Examining RGB–AGL Fusion Stages for High-Resolution Building Extraction Under a Unified SegFormer Framework
content: Accurate building extraction from high-resolution remote sensing imagery remains challenging because RGB data are affected by shadows, roof-material variation, and spectral similarity between buildings and surrounding impervious surfaces. Above-ground-level (AGL) rasters provide complementary geometric cues, but the effect of fusion location remains dependent on model design and domain conditions. This study investigates input-level early fusion, feature-level cross-modal attention (CMA), and prediction-level late fusion within a unified SegFormer framework for RGB–AGL building extraction. Under the fixed tile-level JAX split, in which spatially adjacent tiles may occur in different subsets, the evaluated late-fusion MiT-B2 model achieved a Building IoU of 97.66 ± 0.09% and an F1-score of 98.82 ± 0.02%. In a separate matched three-seed MiT-B2 experiment, CMA improved building IoU from 88.27 ± 0.05% for the RGB baseline to 90.66 ± 0.30%. Zero-shot transfer was strongly target dependent: CMA increased Building IoU from 28.38 ± 3.94% to 49.33 ± 3.66% on Potsdam but decreased it from 59.64 ± 2.60% to 10.27 ± 4.70% on Vaihingen. These findings indicate that RGB–AGL fusion performance depends jointly on fusion-module design, optimization protocol, elevation quality, and source–target domain shift; therefore, no fusion stage should be regarded as universally optimal.
author: Zhengsheng Chen, Junjie Xu, Linyang Li, Yang Cui, Yujie Li

title: Informative Calibration and Cross-Domain Unified Projection With Vision Foundation Models for Remote Sensing Semantic Segmentation
content: Unsupervised domain adaptation for remote sensing semantic segmentation (UDA-RSSS) aims to address the distribution shifts between the source and target domains by transferring knowledge from labeled source domains to unlabeled target domains, which is key to real-world engineering applications, such as urban planning and environmental change detection. Existing UDA-RSSS methods utilize parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) strategies to leverage the knowledge of vision foundation models (VFMs) for adapting well to the target domain from the source domain. However, these methods always accept all calibrated features of VFMs by using PEFT strategies, which ignore whether the calibration is positive or negative, leading to suboptimal performance in the target domain. In this work, relying on VFMs with PEFT strategies, an informative calibration and cross-domain unified projection (ICDP) approach is proposed for UDA-RSSS. The information calibration aims to preserve positive calibration and eliminate negative calibration during the stage of fine-tuning VFMs. The cross-domain unified projection aims to learn a uniform distribution space for calibrated features, thereby reducing the distribution shifts between the source and target domains in the feature space. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed ICDP approach achieves superior performance on multiple UDA-RSSS benchmarks. In addition, the proposed ICDP approach is a plug-and-play, which can apply to existing VFM-based UDA-RSSS methods, achieving significant performance gains.
author: Muxin Liao, Meiying Liao, Yang Chen, Yuting Sun, Wenju Huang, Yinglong Wang, Yingqiong Peng, Wenbin Qian
